title: Derived tensor over R with a complex of A-modules
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a map of commutative rings and let $N$ be a complex of $A$-modules. Regard each commutative ring as a sheaf of rings on the one-point site, so that complexes of modules, K-flat complexes and K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] (which exist [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]), total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the derived categories $D(R)$, $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] apply; a total complex $\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)$ with $E$ a complex of $R$-modules is a complex of $A$-modules through $N$. (1) If $\alpha:E\to E'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of $R$-modules, then $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. (2) There is an exact functor of triangulated categories $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N:D(R)\to D(A)$, the left derived functor of $E\mapsto\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)$, which is everywhere defined and computed by K-flat complexes: for every K-flat resolution $F\to E$ the canonical map $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R N)$ is an isomorphism in $D(A)$, and for two K-flat resolutions of $E$ the resulting isomorphism between the two total complexes in $D(A)$ is canonical (compatible with composition for a third resolution). (3) A morphism $u:N\to N'$ of complexes of $A$-modules induces a natural transformation $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N'$, represented for K-flat $F$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ and compatible with composition of morphisms $u$; if $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every K-flat $F$ and the transformation is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Clause (1) is exactly [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-quasi-iso] on the one-point site, applied with $N$ regarded as a complex of $R$-modules; $\operatorname{Tot}(\alpha\otimes 1_N)$ is moreover $A$-linear, the $A$-action coming through $N$.

Let $\Phi:K(R)\to D(A)$ be $M\mapsto Q_A\operatorname{Tot}(M\otimes_R N)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], a complex of $A$-modules through $N$. It is well defined on the homotopy category: a homotopy $h$ between $f,g:M\to M'$ gives the homotopy $\operatorname{Tot}(h\otimes 1_N)$ between $\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes 1_N)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(g\otimes 1_N)$. For a chain map $f:E\to E'$ the cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(f\otimes 1_N)$ is identified term by term with $\operatorname{Tot}(C(f)\otimes_R N)$: both have the summands $E'^r\otimes N^s$ and $E^{r+1}\otimes N^s$ in total degree $r+s$, with the same block differential and signs; the same reindexing identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(E[1]\otimes_R N)$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_R N)[1]$. Hence $\Phi$ sends cone triangles to cone triangles and is an exact functor of triangulated categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The same computation in the second variable identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R C(u))$ with the cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ for a chain map $u:N\to N'$.

Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to the abelian category of $R$-modules, the exact functor $\Phi$ of Step 2 and $\mathcal P$ the class of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]: hypothesis (1) is [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and hypothesis (2) is Step 1. This gives the everywhere defined exact left derived functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N=L\Phi:D(R)\to D(A)$ with $\varepsilon:L\Phi\circ Q\to\Phi$, $\varepsilon_F$ an isomorphism for K-flat $F$. For a K-flat resolution $s:F\to E$, the canonical map is $\varepsilon_F\circ L\Phi(Q s)^{-1}:E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R N)$, an isomorphism; the isomorphism between the total complexes of two K-flat resolutions is the composite through $E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$, so these isomorphisms are compatible with composition for a third resolution.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (derived-lemma-find-existence-computes with P the K-flat complexes)

proof.text: A morphism $u:N\to N'$ gives chain maps $\operatorname{Tot}(1_M\otimes u)$ of $A$-modules, natural in $M$ and compatible with homotopies, hence a natural transformation $\Phi_N\to\Phi_{N'}$ respecting identities and composites. By the universal property in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] for $(L\Phi_{N'},\varepsilon')$, the composite $L\Phi_N\circ Q\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\Phi_N\to\Phi_{N'}$ factors uniquely through $\varepsilon'$, giving $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N'$; uniqueness gives compatibility with identities and composites, and since $\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon'_F$ are isomorphisms for K-flat $F$ it is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$. If $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $C(u)$ is acyclic (also as a complex of $R$-modules), so $\operatorname{Tot}(C(u)\otimes_R F)$ is acyclic by the definition of K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]; the swap $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ is an isomorphism of total complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(C(u)\otimes_R F)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R C(u))$, and Step 2 identifies the latter with the cone of $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every K-flat $F$, and since every object of $D(R)$ is isomorphic to some $QF$ with $F$ K-flat [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the transformation is an isomorphism.
